title: Amphitheatre of El Djem (Thysdrus)
summary: The amphitheatre at El Djem in Tunisia, ancient Thysdrus, has main axes of 147.90 by 122.20 m and rises 36 m. Tunisia's heritage service says it was built between 238 and 250 AD, while the Princeton Encyclopedia of Classical Sites favours 230–238 and the emperor Gordian I. It has been a World Heritage Site since 1979.

uncertainty.note: The Tunisian ministry gives 238–250 AD; the Princeton Encyclopedia says no inscription survives and favours 230–238, so start allows 8 years earlier. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: Constructed in the period from 238 to 250 AD

reviewer_note: Shape choice: arena (elliptical amphitheatre), axes and height from the Tunisian ministry page. Figures differ slightly by publisher: Princeton gives about 148 x 122 m, arena about 65 x 39 m and seats rising about 36 m; the ministry gives 147.90 x 122.20 m and arena 64 x 39 m. Least sure: the construction date, which no inscription fixes.
